info.title: Kedak Card API
info.summary: Backend API for the Kedak Card metal card conversion storefront.
info.description:
Demo contract for the API the Kedak Card frontend needs. It mirrors what the app implements today: accounts (email + Google), the finish catalog with stock, the artwork library, artwork uploads, the compatibility check, cart validation, checkout, guest and registered order management, cancellations, refunds, policies and staff operations.

**Status:** design/demo. No server implements this yet — the frontend currently uses local preview stores (`src/services/auth.ts`, `src/stores/orders.ts`).

**Payments:** Stripe is not connected. Orders are created with `payment.status = not-collected`; a payment step will be added later.

**Money:** all amounts are integers in minor units (cents) with an ISO 4217 currency, e.g. `{ "amount": 14900, "currency": "USD" }` = $149.00.

**Errors:** every error uses RFC 9457 problem details (`application/problem+json`) with a stable machine-readable `code`.

**Business rules (from `src/utils/orderPolicy.ts`):**
- Cancel: allowed while the order is `awaiting-card`, `card-received` or `assessed` (before conversion). Full refund; a held original card is returned.
- Refund: requested after confirmed delivery, within **21 days (3 weeks)**. Up to the order total, confirmed after the returned card is inspected.
- Checkout: every item must be customised and its finish in stock.

Security: never send or store PINs, CVVs or full card numbers.

post.summary: Validate a cart and price it
post.description: The cart lives in the browser. Call this before showing checkout: it re-prices items and reports blocking issues. `canCheckout` is true only when every item is customised and its finish is in stock.

issues.message: Signature is out of stock. Switch to another finish or remove this item.

post.description:
Works for guests and signed-in customers. If a bearer token is sent, the order is also linked to that account. The response includes an `orderAccessToken` so a guest can manage the order straight away.

Payment: Stripe isn't connected yet, so orders are created with `payment.status = not-collected`.

post.summary: Find an order with reference + email (guests)
post.description: Both values must match. To avoid revealing which orders exist, a wrong reference and a wrong email return the same 404. Rate limited.

200.description: Order found; returns the order and a scoped access token.

get.description: Allowed for the owning account (bearer token) or a guest holding this order's access token.

get.summary: What can the customer do with this order now?
get.description: Server-side source of truth for the Cancel / Request refund actions and their explanations.

cancellation.message: Your card is already being converted, so this order can’t be cancelled. If something’s wrong once it arrives, you can request a refund.

refund.message: You can request a refund once your card has been delivered.

post.description: Allowed while the order is `awaiting-card`, `card-received` or `assessed`. Sets status to `cancelled`, starts a full refund (`refund.state = pending`) and, if we hold the original card, schedules its return.

Allowed for `delivered` orders within 21 days (3 weeks) of confirmed delivery. Sets status to `refund-requested` (`refund.state = requested`). We email return instructions; the refund (up to the order total) is confirmed after inspection.

get.description: Orders placed while signed in or with the account's email, newest first.

parameters.name: refundState
parameters.description: e.g. `requested` to find refunds awaiting review.

post.summary: Move an order to its next fulfilment stage (staff)
post.description: Allowed transitions: awaiting-card → card-received → assessed → in-production → dispatched → delivered. Setting `delivered` records `deliveredAt` (confirmed delivery), which starts the 21-day refund window.

post.summary: Approve, decline or complete a refund (staff)
post.description: `approve` (after inspection, optionally a partial amount up to the order total) → `complete` once paid out sets status `refunded`. `decline` returns the order to `delivered` with an explanation.
